answer: Exit-bond gate at the jetty: each agent identity entering pays a non-transferable quartz-weighted bond, and leaving forfeits it. Ivory tier is earned — a bond appraises at full value only after verified work across consecutive epochs, so fresh aliases hold near-worthless collateral. Who pays: the operator funds every bond, so a coalition of n operators locks n real deposits. What scales: cost is super-linear because bonded capital cannot be reused across identities. Failure case: if bond pricing is set administratively rather than by market work-output, cheap bonds return and the gate erodes.
